name: the circling queen
description: Chess, except that the queen no longer runs in straight lines. The circling queen starts as a queen does, one square in any of the eight directions, but every further square turns her an eighth of a turn the same way, clockwise or anticlockwise as she chooses: north, then north-east, then east, then south-east, and so on, a path that curls round in a small circle of up to seven squares and never comes back to where it began. She may stop anywhere along it, and like a queen she is stopped by the first piece on a square she lands on, taking it if it is an enemy's. Next to her, she moves as a queen does; two or three squares away she reaches squares no queen could, a knight's square among them, and she has lost the long straight lines a queen pins and skewers along. What that changes is where the strongest piece belongs. A queen in the corner of the board still commands a diagonal; this one, far from the action, commands almost nothing, so she has to be brought close, where her curling paths cover a cluster of squares round her and a single piece in the way bends her elsewhere. The decision the game keeps forcing is how near to bring a queen without lines, and how to keep her out of reach of the pieces she is drawn among. Everything else is chess.

provenance.source: docs/plan-pieces-moves.md, T3: the showcase for riders whose path circles (section 5.7, C1)
provenance.history: C1 of docs/plan-pieces-moves.md section 5.7, pre-registered 2026-10-25 before the rule was built: chess (4c1922ffae26) with the queen's slide given path: circle, her own eight directions walked round as a ring of one-square steps, one key on the calibration baseline so a visitor sees what a circling path does. Registered over the fallback, the rose queen, by the rule written before the draft read (C1 unless its self-play at 6400 nodes ran a median under 30 plies or under half decisive; it ran 133 plies, 0.85 decided). Nothing was tunable; the mechanics are T1's test spec tests/_path_ring.json, archived as registered, with the piece named circling queen (the test spec calls it ring queen) and drawn as a queen, a choice made before any measured game.
